To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) patients and their wives were more likely to report a negative family environment than the comparison couples, and (b) high-functioning patients and their wives reported more positive family environments than did their low-functioning counterparts.

the family environment of psychiatric patients and their spouses differs from that of the normative comparison couples in that the former report less cohesion, expressiveness and recreation, and the patients and their spouses are more discrepant in their reports of family environment than the comparison couples.

the perceived family environments among psychiatric patients and wives were consistently less positive than normative comparison couples, that patients' and wives' perceptions of family environment were often discrepant, and that low-functioning patients' wives perceived less cohesion and expressiveness in the family than high-functioning patients' spouses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the family's role in the recovery process.
the family environment of psychiatric inpatients.
the relationship between the family environment and the outcome of psychiatric treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

family environment is important in understanding the recovery process for psychiatric patients and their families, and that family environment may be an important factor in the recovery process for patients with thought disorders.
family environment is not an important variable in the recovery of psychiatric patients.
family environment does not seem to be an important factor in recovery from psychiatric illness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the family environment of psychiatric patients is not as supportive and cohesive as that of normal couples.
family contact, especially positive, can help the patient to recover.
patients who have more positive family relationships are better able to function in the community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
family members are important to the recovery process and should be included in treatment planning.
patients and their families need to be engaged and supported in their recovery.
family members of people who have experienced a mental health crisis may be able to help their loved ones by helping them feel supported and loved.
